evaluation_configuration.benchmark_state_loader_note: The LIBERO checkout has a pre-existing local change to torch.load(..., weights_only=False) for trusted numpy init-state files. Its file timestamp is 2026-09-21, before both evaluations; it does not change task mapping or initial-state selection.
evaluation_configuration.noted_code_path_difference: The completion runner wraps predict_action in torch.inference_mode; the earlier runner relies on the model generation path. Both call predict_action with do_sample=False and use the same evaluation configuration.

configuration_mismatches: Training used double_quant=false, while both evaluation launches used the evaluator default double_quant=true. This is a measured configuration mismatch, not a demonstrated cause of the closed-loop result.
Local training used 3500 updates, effective batch 16, and 4-bit NF4; the official fine-tuning recipe uses 50000 steps, global batch 128, and no quantization.
The local training W&B token accuracy is a training-monitor metric; it is not held-out accuracy or LIBERO success rate.

An existing 24-frame official-checkpoint diagnostic is much stronger than the local adapter on those same training-distribution frames, and a separate official task0 control succeeds on 1/2 fixed states. These small controls support investigating local policy quality but do not replace the full-suite run or isolate a single cause.
